Latin word

labōrō

labōrō, labōrāre, labōrāvī, labōrātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be concerned, be bothered; to labour, toil, work hard; suffer from, be troubled by; be in trouble, be in difficulties; work, toil; also be in difficulty

In this lexicon

  • care

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.3: nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs; Traupman 108: nōn labōrō, for “no sweat”; Cic. Rosc. Am. 97: cujus manū sit percussus, nōn labōrō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 103: I don’t mind if …, nōn labōrō sī …

  • labour

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.121: sēsē sibi labōrāre (Lewis & Short)

  • suffer

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.26.1: graviter ex intestīnīs labōrārem; Cic. Fam. 9.23: ex pedibus labōrārēs; Traupman 56, 64, 387; Traupman 326

  • trouble

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.3: in rē autem familiārī … valdē labōrāmus; Traupman 110, 398

  • work

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 408

Examples

  • nūllā in rē jam tē festīnāre volō; nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs

    I don’t want you to hurry over anything now; all I care about is that you get well.Cic. Fam. 16.4.3
